question: On previously frozen fixed reads, does the utility-trained gate's choice of one 1024-key group to remove improve Dice relative to control choices? This is a retrospective selection among already computed masks, not an online or propagated system.
selection: For each read, choose the single group with the lowest label-free score from the frozen utility-trained, uniform, occupancy-trained, RGB, shuffled, and source-age scores. Stable ties select the lowest group index. Each selected arm removes exactly 1024 keys; compare on the same read and report the arithmetic mean of all five deletion arms as a random-group expectation. No target label influences the choice.
outcomes: Use independently audited saved masks and labels. Report per-sequence present-frame Dice, paired Dice differences from the random-group expectation, and empty-frame false alarms. The no-op is not an equal-key comparator. Do not use ground-truth oracle group choices as an inference method.
limitations: All data and outcomes were previously inspected, utility-trained seq2/3/4 were training data, seq9/10 had been examined and are not independent confirmation, patient independence is unknown, and groups share each read. Local selection effects do not establish video propagation improvements or independent token utility. Historical inference-time Lean usage and distributed baselines are not available for these group-score inputs; earlier priority fixed-read results are separate. No new threshold or redetection.
